strait-of-hormuz.summary: Effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since 28 Feb: Iran requires permits and fees through its Strait Authority, a US blockade of Iranian ports has been in force since 14 July, and attacks on ships continue. Independent Kpler data showed 33.7 mb of crude leaving the strait in the week from 20 Sep, against ~105 mb a week before the war. Many tankers sail with transponders off, so independent counts are partial.

bab-el-mandeb.summary: The Houthis have enforced a 'ban' on Saudi-linked shipping since 20 July, hitting ships (Tihamah 12 Aug, Bahri VLCC off Yanbu 24 Aug) and seizing Mocha and Red Sea islands on 10-11 Sep. Tanker transits fell sharply; overall transits were ~15% below pre-ban levels by late August.

suez-canal.summary: Suez transits were about 36% below normal in late August but 30% higher year on year and recovering, with some VLCCs rerouting via Suez/SUMED.

turkish-straits.summary: Since 8 Aug Turkey has not issued Dardanelles transit permits for commercial ships bound for Novorossiysk (and reportedly Ukraine), after attacks on Turkish-owned vessels in the Black Sea; traffic to Bulgarian and Turkish ports continues.

east-west-pipeline.summary: Shut 11 Sep after drone strikes on pumping stations (launched from Iraq); restarted around 21-22 Sep at a reduced rate, per sources cited by Reuters. Pre-attack it carried ~4-5 mb/d of Hormuz-bypass crude to Yanbu.

yanbu-terminal.summary: Saudi Arabia's main Hormuz-bypass outlet is under Houthi missile and drone threat (intercepts on 24 Sep) and subject to a declared Houthi ban on Saudi-linked shipping. Exports dropped while the East-West pipeline was shut (11–22 Sep). France is sending air defences.

ras-laffan-lng.summary: Two of 14 LNG trains and a GTL plant were destroyed on 19 Mar (12.8 mtpa, ~17% of capacity, 3-5 years to repair). The rest of the plant runs at minimum because exports depend on Hormuz; Qatar resumed limited tanker movements in September.

kharg-island.summary: The terminal was intact after US strikes on military targets (14 Mar). Iranian exports have been under a US naval blockade since 14 July, and the US struck an Iranian tanker off Kharg on 5 Sep. Independent data on remaining Iranian loadings is limited.

abqaiq-oil.summary: Drone strikes from Iraq on 27 Jul damaged the Abqaiq processing plant (~7 mb/d), which handles Ghawar crude; the IEA cited them among causes of Saudi supply falling to 6 mb/d in August. Current repair status not verified.

ghawar-oil.summary: Saudi crude supply was 6.0 mb/d in August (IEA), the lowest in over three decades, as exports are squeezed by Hormuz, the Red Sea blockade and attacks. September exports were recovering via Gulf terminals (>4 mb/d provisional, Kpler).

ras-tanura-terminal.summary: Loadings are constrained by the Hormuz situation. Ship-tracking (MarineTraffic, TankerTrackers.com) showed Ras Tanura and Ju'aymah loading ~12–14 mb on 21 Sep, the busiest day since before the war.

fujairah.summary: The UAE's main outlet outside Hormuz, fed by the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline (~1.5 mb/d), has been attacked repeatedly (14 and 16 Mar, 4 May). Kpler data showed exports rising to 1.62 mb/d in March from 1.17 mb/d in February as volumes were rerouted there. Status after May not verified.

rumaila-oil.summary: Southern Iraqi output was slashed in March (Basra Oil Co. ~3.3 to ~0.9 mb/d; force majeure 20 Mar). Iraq said exports reached ~2 mb/d in August, the highest since the war began, mostly via Hormuz and partly via Ceyhan.

cpc-pipeline.summary: Drone attacks on tankers at the CPC terminal (17-20 Jul) halted loadings on 22 Jul and forced Kazakh output cuts. Loadings resumed but were below normal as of 8 Aug; Ukraine has since agreed with the US not to target CPC-linked shipping. Turkish permit limits on Novorossiysk-bound ships add risk.
